  THRUSDAY, NOVEMBER 19, 2020
  7:00 P.M.

The City of San Marino appreciates your attendance. Citizens’ interest provides the Design Review Committee
with valuable information regarding issues of the community.

Regular Meetings are held on the 1st and 3rd Wednesday of every month.

In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, any person with a disability who requires a modification
or accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the City Clerk’s Office at (626) 300-0705
at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

  PURSUANT TO EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-33-20 AND N-29-20

In accordance with the Governor’s Executive Orders N-33-20 and N-29-20, and given the health risk associated
with COVID-19, this public hearing will be conducted via teleconference/virtual meeting, without a physical
location from which members of the public may attend. Members of the public may access the meeting
electronically via the zoom.us teleconference module (Computer for Video Streaming) and web-streamed live
at https://us02web.zoom.us/j/89083355363
Meeting ID: 890 8335 5363

Members of the public may participate in the public hearing by submitting written comments to Eva Choi,
Associate Planner, at echoi@cityofsanmarino.org and Marlon Cervantes, Assistant Planner, at
mcervantes@cityofsanmarino.org. Comments received prior to 4:00 p.m. on the date of the meeting will be
forwarded to the Design Review Committee and included in the public record. Comments submitted after 4:00
p.m. on the date of the meeting must be submitted through Zoom. Please be sure to include your name and
the agenda item you are addressing.

FOR FURTHER INFORMATION, please contact the Planning and Building Division at (626) 300-0700. A
copy of the staff reports under review at this Design Review Committee meeting will be available for public
review by the end of the day on November 13, 2020 on the City’s website at: www.cityofsanmarino.org

CALL TO ORDER

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL:  Chair Joyce Gatsoulis-Batnij, Vice-Chair Peter Wong, Committee Member Raymond
  Cheng, Committee Member Christa Lakon, Committee Member Sharon Mequet,
  Alternate Committee Member Rick Chou and Alternate Committee Member Tony
  Chou

POSTING OF AGENDA

The agenda is posted 72 hours prior to each meeting at the following locations: City Hall, 2200 Huntington
Drive, the Crowell Public Library, 1890 Huntington Drive and the Recreation Department, 1560 Pasqualito
Drive. The agenda is also posted on the City’s Website: http://www.cityofsanmarino.org

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Section 54954.3 of the Brown Act provides an opportunity for members of the public to address the Design
Review Committee on any item of interest to the public, before or during the Design Review Committee’s
consideration of the item, that is within the subject matter jurisdiction of the Design Review Committee.

  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  1. DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC20-30
  1470 VIRGINIA RD., (CENTURY WINNER, INC./TYLER+KELLY ARCHITECTURE)
  The applicant proposes to construct front yard fencing, a driveway gate, a pedestrian gate, and pilasters
  with lighting.
  (Required Action Date: 12-12-2020)

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the Design Review Committee 1) find that the proposed
  fencing, gates and pilasters are exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines Section 15303; 2) find that the proposed fencing, gates and
  pilasters are compatible with the Spanish Colonial Revival residence and other fences and gates found
  on the Block; and 3) approve the proposed project with a condition to eliminate the lighting fixtures
  on the pilasters.

  2. DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC20-60
  1045 ROSALIND RD., (CHEN)
  The applicant proposes to make exterior modifications to an existing two-story residence.
  (Required Action Date: 12-12-2020)

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the Design Review Committee 1) find that the proposed
  exterior modifications project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  pursuant to ·state CEQA Guidelines Section 15301(e)(1) – Existing Facilities; 2) find that the proposed
  exterior modification project is incompatible with the legal neighborhood and with the existing
  structures; and 3) continue the project.

  OTHER MATTERS
 DESIGN REVIEW COMMITTEE AGENDA – NOVEMBER 19, 2020  PAGE 3 OF 3

OPEN FORUM

This is an opportunity for future applicants to informally present preliminary design concepts for feedback from
members of the DRC. Comments received are based on members not having visited the site and neighborhood.
Therefore, positive comments should not be perceived as preliminary approval of a project but rather as a tool
in facilitating a project through the Design Review process. No more than two DRC members may participate
in Open Forum discussions. Applications that have been heard by the DRC may not be discussed during Open
Forum.

PUBLIC WRITINGS DISTRIBUTED

All public writings distributed by the City of San Marino to at least a majority of the Design Review Committee
regarding any item on this agenda will be made available at the Public Counter at City Hall located at 2200
Huntington Drive, San Marino, California.

ADJOURNMENT

The San Marino Design Review Committee will adjourn to the next regular meeting to be held on Wednesday,
December 2, 2020 at 7:00 p.m., pursuant to Executive Order N-29-20 issued by Governor Gavin Newsom, the
meeting will be held through teleconference.

APPEALS

There is a fifteen day appeal period for all applications. All appeals should be filed with the Planning and Building
Department. Please contact the Planning and Building Department for further information.

SUBJECT:  DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC20-30
  1470 VIRGINIA RD., (CENTURY WINNER INC./
  TYLER+KELLY ARCHITECTURE)

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to construct front yard fencing, a driveway gate, a pedestrian gate, and pilasters with
lighting.

The property is under construction for a two-story Spanish Colonial Revival residence designed by Mr. Robert
Tyler, a Pasadena based architect. Mr. Tyler has been retained to design the proposed front yard
improvements given his understanding of the site conditions and the design elements of the residence. The
applicant wishes to install front yard improvements as part of the final construction phase for the property.

TREE PRESERVATION

This project will not remove or relocate any trees.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION

The project is Categorically Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to
CEQA Guidelines Section 15303(e) because the project involves accessory structures (fencing and
gates).

PROJECT HISTORY

November 4, 2020 – Agenized for the meeting but was not heard due to time limit. The item was re-
scheduled to a special meeting.
November 19, 2020 – First hearing before the DRC
December 12, 2020 – Required action date
 NEIGHBOR APPROVAL/OBJECTION LETTERS

Approve – 4
Object – 0
No response – 5

DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS

San Marino City Code Section 23.13.04G identifies separate design review findings relating to the
approval of fence, gates, walls and pilasters. The Design Review Committee may not reduce the
maximum permitted height, increase the minimum required setback or decrease the maximum
permitted opacity of any fence, gate, yard wall or retaining wall located in a side yard adjacent to a
street; except, that the Design Review Committee can increase the minimum setback for a gate
providing access to a driveway in order to protect pedestrian or vehicular traffic.

The DRC shall approve the application for the side yard wall adjacent to a street if it finds all of the
following to be true:

  1. That the proposed fence, gate, pilaster, yard wall or retaining wall is
  architecturally compatible with the existing residence.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO  ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The proposed fencing, gates, and pilasters are architecturally compactible with the
  Spanish Revival home. The pilasters’ color and finish are consistent with the residence. The
  proposed fencing is hidden behind the existing hedge, the gates and pilasters are located at an
  angle to minimize its visual appearance from the street.

  2. That the proposed fence, gate, pilaster, yard wall or retaining wall is consistent
  with the size and location of fences, gates, pilasters, yard walls and retaining walls
  on the block on which the property is located.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO  ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  The Municipal Code defines Block as the property abutting on one side of a street and lying
  between the two (2) nearest intersecting or intercepting streets or between the termination
  of such street and the nearest intersecting or intercepting street.

  Comments: The property is located on Virginia Road across from Lacy Park, there are only
  two properties located within the definition of the Block, these are 1505 Euston Road and
  1464 Virginia Road. Both properties are corner lot, equipped with yard fencing and driveway
  gate. It should be noted that the driveway gate is located along the side yard abutting Virginia
  Road for 1505 Euston Road due to the structure’s orientation on the corner lot. However,
  staff did not observe exterior lighting fixtures installed in the same manner as the proposed
  ones on the pilasters, thus cannot support the lighting fixtures.

  2
   3. That the proposed fence, gate, pilaster, yard wall or retaining wall preserves site
  lines and is otherwise located in a manner not to create a hazard to pedestrian or
  vehicular traffic.

  Staff can make this finding: ☒YES  ☐NO  ☐ NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The wrought iron fencing along the front property line provides an eighteen (18)
  inches setback from the property line and is screened by existing hedges. The driveway gate
  and pilasters are setback approximately twenty-eight (28) feet from the curb, staff finds this
  distance to be sufficient to accommodate a vehicle queuing on the driveway without disrupting
  oncoming traffic or causing hazardous conditions to drivers and pedestrians.

RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Design Review Committee 1) find that the proposed fencing, gates and
pilasters are exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to State CEQA
Guidelines Section 15303; 2) find that the proposed fencing, gates and pilasters are compatible with
the Spanish Colonial Revival residence and other fences and gates found on the Block; and 3) approve
the proposed project with a condition to eliminate the lighting fixtures on the pilasters.

 FROM:  Eva Choi, Associate Planner
 DATE:  November 19, 2020
 SUBJECT: DESIGN REVIEW CASE NO. DRC20-60
  1045 ROSALIND RD., (CHEN)

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant proposes to make exterior modifications to an existing two-story residence.

The exterior modifications include replacement of all windows and doors, removal of some of
the decorative half-timbering, re-stucco with a smooth Santa Barbara finish, changing the roof
shape over the master bathroom from a dome/bell shape to a pyramid turret shape.

The project includes a second story balcony extension that is not covered by a roof and does
not change the appearance of the structure as viewed from the street, thus the balcony
extension is not subject to design review.

BACKGROUND ON THE PROPERTY

The current owners purchased the property in December 2017. On February 21, 2018, City
staff observed that windows were removed without permit. City staff issued violation notice to
the property owner and subsequently a permit was issued on September 17, 2018 with penalty
fee for extensive interior upgrade and replacement of windows and doors on the residence and
the guest house. The building permit and related photographs which demonstrate the original
windows details are provided as Attachment 3.

At the beginning of 2020, the property owner’s representative contacted planning staff to
submit an application for exterior modifications to the structure. Nearby residents have
submitted complaints to the City about the lack of property maintenance and the prolonged
construction project.
 TREE PRESERVATION

There are no proposed tree removals as part of this project.

ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION

The project is Categorically Exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act pursuant to
CEQA Guidelines Section 15301(e)(1) – Existing Facilities.

The existing two-story Tudor Revival structure was designed by Mr. Tom Nott, a local
architect based in South Pasadena, and constructed in 1977 to 1978. The owner on building
permit record was Imperial Development, a company based in Sherman Oaks, California.
A recently completed City Wide Historic Survey prepared by Architectural Resources Group
(ARG) did not include the subject property on the list of eligible properties for listing as a
historic resource given the age of the structure and the status of the architect and builder.
Thus, the proposed project will not result in a substantial adverse change to a historic resource
under the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA).

PROJECT HISTORY

November 4, 2020 – Agenized for the meeting but was not heard due to time limit. The item
was re-scheduled to a special meeting.
November 19, 2020 – First hearing before the DRC
December 12, 2020 – Required action date

NEIGHBOR APPROVAL/OBJECTION LETTERS

Approve – 5
Object – 2
No response – 6

DESIGN REVIEW FINDINGS

Section 23.15.08 of the San Marino City Code states that the DRC shall approve the application
if it finds all of the following to be true:

  1. That the proposed structure is compatible with the neighborhood.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐YES  ☒NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  2
   Comments: The legal neighborhood comprises of homes in traditional architectural
  styles, with materials and details that are authentic to its period of construction. The
  proposed changes to the stucco finished texture, reduction in the decorative half-
  timbering, and window treatments will remove visually distinguishable features of the
  residence and renders it incompatible with the neighborhood.

2. That the proposed structure is designed and will be developed in a manner
  which balances the reasonable expectation of privacy of persons residing on
  contiguous properties with the reasonable expectations of the applicants to
  develop their property within the restrictions of this Code.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐YES  ☐NO  ☒NOT APPLICABLE

3. In the case of a building addition, the proposal is compatible with the existing
  building which includes the rooflines.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐YES  ☒NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: Staff finds the proposed master bathroom’s roof shape change from a
  dome/bell shape to a pyramid turret shape compatible with the roof form of the
  residence. Staff is unable to support the remainder of the project as it deviates from
  traditional elements associated with the Tudor Revival design.

  Although the second-floor rear-facing balcony is not subject to design review, staff
  wishes to point out that the concept of a balcony to “square off” the structure takes
  away the asymmetrical form and whimsical nature that the Tudor design is known for.

4. That the colors and materials are consistent and match the existing building
  or structure.

  Staff can make this finding: ☐YES  ☒NO  ☐NOT APPLICABLE

  Comments: The proposed roofing material is a simulated wood shake product from the
  City’s Pre-Approved material list. The new windows are Marvin aluminum clad wood
  product, however the windows lack decorative element and the operations being single
  hung and fixed are inconsistent with the Tudor structure. Typical Tudor styled home
  consists of tall windows with multiple panes with diamond-shaped leaded glass or other
  forms of decorative front-facing windows. The new entry door is incompatible with the
  style of the home. The proposed roof fascia board is made of a synthetic/composite
  material which is discouraged by the Residential Design Guidelines and it is an
  inappropriate material choice for a structure in the Estate District. The earth-tone
  exterior color scheme is appropriate, however the Santa Barbara variable stucco finish
  as noted on Sheet A4.0 is not compatible with the traditional exterior treatments
  existed on the home as part of the original design.

  3
 RECOMMENDATION

Staff recommends that the Design Review Committee 1) find that the proposed exterior
modifications project is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
pursuant to ·state CEQA Guidelines Section 15301(e)(1) – Existing Facilities; 2) find that the
proposed exterior modifications project is incompatible with the legal neighborhood and with
the existing structures; and 3) continue the proposed project.
